title: Multi-step native IDP interaction
prerequisites: These bindings target classic MCSDK with KSSIDP; standalone IDPSDK needs its own adapter and is not interchangeable.
Native flow chosen explicitly and its wrapper/delegate contract identified.
UI can present successive field/challenge requests and cancellation.
sequence: Retain the same interaction/session context for successive callbacks.
Render only the fields requested by the current callback.
Submit the response through the corresponding delegate/continuation.
Distinguish continuation, cancellation, HTTP failure, event failure and terminal success.
Clear sensitive input and pending state on terminal completion.
expected_result: A flow requesting more than one screen can finish.
checklist: A flow requesting more than one screen can finish.
Cancellation is processed and does not leave the app waiting indefinitely.
A network failure is distinguished from SDK rejection.
failure_handling: Native does not imply single-page. Do not reject a flow because an example expects one dictionary.
Do not log callback bodies containing passwords, codes or tokens.

platform_notes.android: KssIdpModel and MultiflowActionType separate multi-step actions from simpler credential mappings.
platform_notes.ios: KssIdpModel uses appDelegate callbacks and handles success, letter-sent, event-failure, request-failure and biometric-error results distinctly.

qualification.note: Examples compile against the exact classic MCSDK/KSSIDP artifact in each example validation record. Compilation and synthetic diagnostics do not qualify a complete live app flow.

validation.scope: Compiled and linked as part of a fresh native app; no live flow acceptance.
